# the contributor audit: individual potentials and exact endpoint support credit

Source: `candidate f5316a23a6622c7a`, Sections 1–9 after correction of (33). Full independent audit: **PASS**. the contributor reran the expanded verifier: 215 exact checks pass, including independent edge integration of the corrected endpoint potential.

The harmonic summation rule uses one common boundary measure, fixed nonnegative profiles, and a cone closed under nonnegative sums. All cross terms are nonnegative. Approximate individual suprema suffice for a strict below-target descent; test attainment is unnecessary. The fixed deepest-face witness theorem supplies its separate parity-bounded count when the selected circuits have the required regularity. The sum lemma itself does not provide an individual efficiency theorem or a nonsmooth allocation rule.

The full convex-test calibration on each triangle facet follows from the midpoint convexity inequality integrated over the three equal subintervals. Applying it to every facet and binary fiber gives the exact upper bounds; base hinges attain them. The common critical cap masses, coarea weights and section centroids are actual simplex data. The oblique truncated-triangle constant-potential calculation retains all four fiber edges and its strict algebraic sign.

The signed radial identity has the correct positive cut-flux term. Its affine-center correction cancels only after invoking the full mixed section centroid at the source. Passing to a positive part retains the extra Xi term. The exact binary-product obstruction therefore validly blocks the entire matching-source radial-hinge cone; it does not block base-localized hinges.

For a heavy profile weight, the actual positive cap-margin hinge has positive boundary integral and is supported inside that cap. An exposed double-captured point also yields a finite shallow hinge of positive boundary integral supported in the double intersection. Compactness and strict incidence justify that localization.

At an exposed base, a sufficiently large FINITE base penalty isolates the fiber uniformly over unit normals. Choosing c in the actual fiber makes its boundary radial velocity nonnegative. The divergence calculation gives the exact numerator d C_p+B_p-T_p dot c; compact support maximization gives (30) with h_Kp(-T_p). It is an attained potential, including if the optimizer c lies on the fiber boundary.

For {-1,0,1}, actual section-centroid stationarity forces equal endpoint section weights. The integer-normal terms cancel only in their SUM, yielding the paired support identity (31). No claim that y lies in the midpoint body is made. The support correction remains directional and cannot be replaced by an assumed scalar gain.

the contributor caught an error in the original numerical example: T=0 did not imply B_p=0. In that example B_p=4 e t^2 p/(6t-1). The source now retains it and gives E_-=[delta-2 e t^2/(6t-1)]/|A|=12368000000/27259241181, still strictly above 4/9. Independent edge integration verifies the corrected numerator and denominator; the previous value delta/|A| is invalid. The general formulas already retained B_p and were unaffected.

The subsequent summed three-fiber formal support identity is a separate extension. The middle-fiber optimizer need not admit convex base localization. No global Gamma-sized lower bound, arbitrary finite-base theorem, or OC conclusion is proved here.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
